likely_official_source_authorities_neede.customs_or_border_authority: Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli (Italian Customs and Monopolies Agency)
likely_official_source_authorities_neede.financial_intelligence_unit_or_aml_autho: Unità di Informazione Finanziaria (UIF, housed at Banca d'Italia)

candidates.expected_difficulty: Medium. No internal research file exists yet — this is a from-scratch intake. Italy's cash-declaration regime sits on top of EU Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 (cross-border cash controls), so both the EU-level instrument and Italy's national implementing authority must be sourced and clearly distinguished from each other.
known_risk_areas: EU-level regulation vs Italy-specific implementing rules must be sourced and cited separately, never merged into one unattributed claim
Italy shares EUR with Germany and France (already published) — its rules must NOT be assumed identical to either published Eurozone entry
Italian-language source translation accuracy

P8E-1 finding (2026-07-24): Italy DOES impose a cash-declaration obligation for movements between Italy and other EU countries (intra-EU), via national Legislative Decree 195/2008, on top of the EU external-border rule (Regulation (EU) 2018/1672; EUR 10 000 or more). The two must be cited separately — the EU instrument for the extra-EU external border, D.Lgs 195/2008 for the Italian intra-EU obligation; both administered by Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli (with Guardia di Finanza), filed at customs offices; penalty EUR 300 up to 40% of the amount exceeding EUR 10 000.

P8E-1 finding: EU 'cash' definition (Regulation (EU) 2018/1672) covers banknotes and coins, cheques, traveller's cheques, prepaid cards and gold; accompanied cash (carrier) is declared, unaccompanied cash (post/freight/courier) is disclosed on customs request; the Regulation applies from 3 June 2021 (repealed Reg 1889/2005). Exact 'EUR 10 000 or more' wording and article numbers to be pinned from the official source at P8E-2.

P8E-1 finding: the Italian DOMESTIC cash-payment ceiling (D.Lgs 231/2007 Art. 49; reportedly EUR 5 000 from 1 Jan 2023 by the 2023 Budget Law — pin the exact current figure at P8E-2) is a domestic payment limit and must NOT be confused with the border cash-declaration threshold.

P8E-1 finding: keep four regimes strictly separate — (a) EU/Italy border cash declaration (ADM); (b) general payment and capital-movement freedom (Banca d'Italia / ECB; no exchange controls; free movement of capital, Art. 63 TFEU); (c) AML reporting (UIF, D.Lgs 231/2007); (d) the domestic cash-payment ceiling. Italy is sourced as its own jurisdiction, not inferred from the published France or Germany entries or a shared EU framework.

P8E-1 environment note: ADM pages 403-block WebFetch and EUR-Lex is JS-gated here; source existence and content were confirmed via official ADM guidance and EC/EUR-Lex summaries, but exact article/page/form-number pinpointing (EU Regulation articles, D.Lgs 195/2008 articles, ADM declaration-form number, current Travellers' Customs Charter version/date, and exact penalty and cash-ceiling figures) is deferred to the P8E-2 publication-candidate review.

P8E-2 outcome (2026-07-24): data/rules/italy.json created (page_status verified, indexing false). CONFIRMED via primary ADM Circular 12/2024: the intra-EU obligation is Art. 3 D.Lgs 195/2008 and the EU-border obligation is Art. 3 Reg (EU) 2018/1672 (EUR 10 000; single ADM form; Art. 28 seizure). Declaration fields are publication-grade and pinpointed. Capital/exchange/resident/non-resident/business/banking fields remain [HARDENING] — TFEU Art. 63 (EUR-Lex) is JS-gated and no claim-specific Banca d'Italia/ECB primary page was obtainable. Per the readiness rule, Italy is HELD at source_review_ready (6 [HARDENING] markers remain); no governance exception. Blocker for P8E-2b: fetch/pin TFEU Art. 63 and claim-specific Banca d'Italia sources for the capital/banking cluster. Penalty figures deliberately not asserted.
